items.followUp: Why does the atomic radius increase down a group in the periodic table?

rubric.why: Additional electron shells down a group increase atomic size and place the valence electrons farther from the nucleus.
rubric.description: States that atomic size increases or valence electrons are farther from the nucleus down a group.

rubric.why: Weaker attraction to the outer electrons makes them easier to lose, increasing the reactivity of metals.
rubric.description: Connects weaker attraction or easier electron loss with increasing metal reactivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the connection to increased reactivity.

modelAnswer: Down a group, atomic size increases and the valence electrons are farther from the nucleus.
The nucleus attracts these electrons less strongly, so they are lost more easily and the reactivity of metals increases.

items.followUp: What happens to the electropositivity of an element when its ionization energy increases?

rubric.why: Electropositivity and ionization energy vary in opposite directions.
rubric.description: States that electropositivity and ionization energy are inversely related.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the inverse relationship.

rubric.why: Low ionization energy means electrons are removed easily, so the element is more electropositive.
rubric.description: Explains the relationship using ease of electron removal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly linking ionization energy with electron loss and electropositivity.

modelAnswer: Electropositivity and ionization energy are inversely related.
An element with low ionization energy loses electrons easily and is highly electropositive; an element with high ionization energy has low electropositivity.

items.followUp: Which contains more molecules: 18 g of water or 18 g of sucrose? Show the calculation.

rubric.why: Nine grams of water is 0.50 mol, which contains 3.01 × 10²³ molecules.
rubric.description: Calculates the amount or number of molecules in the water sample.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for either the correct amount in moles or the correct number of water molecules.

rubric.why: Nine grams of sugar is approximately 0.0263 mol, or 1.58 × 10²² molecules, so the water sample has more molecules.
rubric.description: Calculates the sugar amount and identifies water as having more molecules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct sugar amount or for the correct molecule-count comparison identifying water.

modelAnswer: Given: m(H₂O) = 0.009 kg; M(H₂O) = 0.018 kg mol⁻¹; m(C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) = 0.009 kg; M(C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) = 0.342 kg mol⁻¹.
Formula: n = m / M; number of molecules = n × Nₐ, where Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
For water: n = 0.009 kg / 0.018 kg mol⁻¹ = 0.50 mol.
Number of H₂O molecules = 0.50 mol × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ = 3.01 × 10²³ molecules.
For sugar: n = 0.009 kg / 0.342 kg mol⁻¹ = 0.0263 mol.
Number of sugar molecules = 0.0263 mol × 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹ ≈ 1.58 × 10²² molecules.
Therefore, 9 g of H₂O has more molecules.
